sections.markdown:
## C — Vehicle emergencies, collision response and crash reporting

FACT_ID: sec18-F01 | anchor: A01
Follow the vehicle owner’s recommended maintenance schedule to reduce the likelihood of a breakdown. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0136]

FACT_ID: sec18-F02 | anchor: A01
Never select the ignition’s Lock position while the vehicle is moving because steering can lock and control can be lost. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0136]

FACT_ID: sec18-F03 | anchor: A01
If the brakes stop working, the handbook says pumping the pedal several times may rebuild pressure enough to stop. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0136]

FACT_ID: sec18-F04 | anchor: A01
If pumping failed brakes does not help, the handbook describes applying the parking-brake handle gradually and releasing it if a skid begins. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0136]

FACT_ID: sec18-F05 | anchor: A01
If the preceding brake-failure measures do not work, shift down and look for a safe off-road stopping place. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0136]

FACT_ID: sec18-F06 | anchor: A01
Do not continue driving a vehicle without brakes. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0136]

FACT_ID: sec18-F07 | anchor: A01
Test brakes after deep water because wet brakes can pull sideways or fail to hold. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0136]

FACT_ID: sec18-F08 | anchor: A01
The handbook’s wet-brake drying procedure uses low gear, slow travel and light brake application. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0136]

FACT_ID: sec18-F09 | anchor: A01
During that wet-brake procedure, the handbook says to recheck braking every 200 feet until normal action returns. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0136]

FACT_ID: sec18-F10 | anchor: A01
After leaving the pavement unintentionally, avoid panic or abrupt braking and release the accelerator. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0136]

FACT_ID: sec18-F11 | anchor: A01
If the vehicle runs off the pavement, keep a firm hold on the wheel because uneven forces can twist it. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0136]

FACT_ID: sec18-F12 | anchor: A01
Before attempting to return from the shoulder, the handbook requires vehicle control, speed no greater than 15 mph and a rear-traffic check. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0136]

FACT_ID: sec18-F13 | anchor: A01
When returning to pavement, avoid crossing the center line. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0136]

FACT_ID: sec18-F14 | anchor: A02
If a tire suddenly deflates, hold the wheel firmly, keep a straight course and reduce speed gradually. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0137]

FACT_ID: sec18-F15 | anchor: A02
For a sudden flat tire, the handbook advises releasing the accelerator, braking lightly and moving to a safe place off the roadway if possible. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0137]

FACT_ID: sec18-F16 | anchor: A02
If the engine dies while moving, keep a strong steering grip and pull off the roadway; steering may be harder and the brakes may require greater pedal force. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0137]

FACT_ID: sec18-F17 | anchor: A02
If the headlights suddenly fail, try operating their switch several times. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0137]

FACT_ID: sec18-F18 | anchor: A02
If the switch does not restore headlights, use available hazard, signal or fog lights and leave the roadway as soon as possible. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0137]

FACT_ID: sec18-F19 | anchor: A02
If the accelerator sticks, keep watching the road, shift promptly to neutral, pull aside safely and then switch off the engine. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0137]

FACT_ID: sec18-F20 | anchor: A03
Smoke from under the hood calls for getting off the roadway. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0138]

FACT_ID: sec18-F21 | anchor: A03
If a train approaches a vehicle stalled on the tracks, leave the vehicle and move far away from the tracks in the general direction the train approaches from to avoid collision debris. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0138]

FACT_ID: sec18-F22 | anchor: A03
When a collision threatens, the handbook identifies stopping, steering away or accelerating as possible responses. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0138]

FACT_ID: sec18-F23 | anchor: A03
Read the owner’s manual for the vehicle’s ABS operation. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0138]

FACT_ID: sec18-F24 | anchor: A03
For an emergency stop with functioning ABS, press the brake pedal firmly and keep pressure on it even if the pedal pushes back. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0138]

FACT_ID: sec18-F25 | anchor: A03
Without ABS, apply emergency braking as strongly as possible without locking the wheels. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0138]

FACT_ID: sec18-F26 | anchor: A03
If non-ABS braking locks the wheels and starts a skid, release brake pressure quickly and reapply after the skid ends, repeating until stopped. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0138]

FACT_ID: sec18-F27 | anchor: A03
When steering to avoid a collision, hold the wheel with both hands and remain ready to control the vehicle after the evasive move. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0138]

FACT_ID: sec18-F28 | anchor: A03
Steer toward the intended safe path rather than letting the first evasive movement lead into another collision. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0138]

Misconceptions: Preserve the source’s conditions, exceptions and may-versus-must distinction when recalling a rule.
Mnemonics: Use “cause, condition, consequence” as an authored cue for reviewing each cited rule.
Glossary: The key source terms are retained in the individual facts and their domain labels.
Dynamic facts: Contact details, provider lists and current service availability require fresh confirmation and stay outside the stable fact set.
